findings.quote: The example runs in the test image use a project that already pins all three, so there the install step is not needed.
findings.why: Describes one particular test image's preinstalled Julia project as if it were part of using the solver; a standalone user has no such image.

findings.quote: Each `AllDifferent` over expressions is checked in the test image: `[q[i] + i ...] in MOI.AllDifferent(n)` is OPTIMAL when the queens fit (n = 4, 8) and INFEASIBLE for n = 3, so the constraint is enforced, not ignored.
findings.why: Refers to verification done 'in the test image', a specific test setup, rather than to the solver's own behaviour.

findings.quote: | Runner shows `exit code 1` with only `[16] _start()` and `in expression starting at ...` | the runner prints the last lines of the Julia stack, not the error | run `julia model.jl <instance>` yourself and read the first line of stderr, which starts with `ERROR:` |
findings.why: Describes what 'the runner' shows and truncates, which only makes sense for someone whose model is executed by a benchmark runner.

findings.quote: - Print a status line for the non-solution cases (`{"status": "unsatisfiable"}` or similar) and exit with code 1 when the optimum is not proven, with the message on `stderr`.
findings.why: Prescribes a JSON status record and an exit-code convention for unproven optima, an output protocol for a reading program rather than anything JuMP or HiGHS requires.

findings.quote: - Print one line per solution when enumerating, so the output can be split on newlines.
findings.why: Together with the one-line JSON object at line 162 this is a JSONL solution-record convention for something else to parse.
